title: Returnees protest quarantine at Mapanga Prison Training College
location: Mapanga Prison Training College and nearby Blantyre–Zomba Road, Blantyre
scope: Local action at a government quarantine site and adjacent road; relation to other returnee actions is unknown.
organizer: Malawian returnees recently arrived from South Africa; no organizer named.
participants_original: “only few individuals” (prison spokesperson, as reported by Face of Malawi; no number)
threshold_50_evidence: Face of Malawi quotes a prison spokesperson saying “only few individuals” were perpetuating the riot, but gives no number. The broader arrival cohort was 518 according to Nyasa Times/Face and about 600 according to VOA; neither is protest attendance. The >=50 threshold remains unverified.

occurrence.summary: Nyasa Times and Face of Malawi report the Jan 10 Mapanga protest/riot and adjacent road block; VOA provides a later independent account but remains search-only. Malawi24 archive lists a Jan 10 article; The Nation later references a Mapanga riot without precise date.

start_date.summary: Face of Malawi Jan 11 says the fracas erupted “yesterday,” Jan 10; VOA calls the incident Sunday, Jan 10. Nyasa Times publication date is Jan 11 but not used as event date.

end_date.summary: Police tear gas restored order, but no physical end time is given.

location.summary: Mapanga Prison Training College in Blantyre and the adjacent Blantyre–Zomba Road.

organizer.summary: Recent returnees from South Africa; no organizer or leader named.

demands.summary: Return of passports and immediate release to go home, protesting quarantine. VOA additionally reports complaints about living conditions and lack of advance notice.

participants.summary: Face of Malawi quotes a prison spokesperson that only “few individuals” perpetuated riots but gives no number. The 518/approximately 600 returnees are the overall cohorts, not participants.

protester_violence.summary: Reports attribute blocked road, smashed vehicles and fires/damage at facility to some returnees.

state_response.summary: Police used tear gas to end/restore order (crowd_dispersal yes). VOA reports 39 returnees arrested/charged, but its page remains search_only in this unit; Face of Malawi’s initial spokesperson said none had escaped at that point, while VOA reports about 20 escaped. The Nation later mentions arrests among returnees without linking them precisely to this event. Keep event-specific arrests unknown pending opened evidence. Officials withheld passports and enforced Covid measures; no accommodation. Beatings, killings and shootings not reported.

notes: Reported incident began Jan 10 at a government quarantine site and adjacent public road, demanding passports and release. Attendance remains unverified: Face of Malawi says only “few individuals” rioted; the 518/approximately 600 arrivals are not event counts. VOA reports 20 escapees/39 arrests, which differs from the Jan 11 Face account; preserve the update conflict. The Nation’s Jan 24 article concerns a later cohort and says only that returnees previously rioted at Mapanga and that some people had been arrested; it does not establish that its arrest reference belongs to Jan 10.
open_questions: Verify VOA’s event-specific report of 39 arrests/charges and about 20 escapees against further opened evidence; distinguish groups/timing. Root coordinator reports successful ordinary retrieval outside this unit record.
Determine whether >=50 people actually participated; cohort sizes are not attendance.
Review whether the action at a quarantine facility plus adjacent road qualifies under original event scope.
Clarify physical closure; no end time is reported.

title: CDEDI and Blantyre small-scale business operators’ march
scope: Local city action; relation to a broader small-business campaign is unresolved.
organizer: Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI) and Blantyre Small Scale Business Operators
threshold_50_evidence: No verified numerical count establishes 50 or more people; retain the reported qualitative wording and leave threshold unresolved.

occurrence.summary: Nyasa Times reports that the groups held a peaceful demonstration on Tuesday, Jan 19. The article calls the turnout “dozens,” which does not establish 50.

start_date.summary: The report published Jan 20 explicitly dates the march to Tuesday Jan 19, 2021.

end_date.summary: No physical ending time or date is reported; publication date is not used as episode end.

organizer.summary: CDEDI and Blantyre Small Scale Business Operators.

demands.summary: Collective demands included lowering fuel prices, action on alleged selective justice, delivery of promised jobs, and an expenditure report on cancelled independence celebrations. Land and foreign-trader concerns were raised by one participant and are not coded as the collective platform.

participants.summary: Nyasa Times describes “dozens” at the Jan 19 march. No exact count or clear lower bound of 50.

protester_violence.summary: The report explicitly characterizes the demonstration as peaceful.

state_response.summary: No event-specific formal state reception, arrests, beatings, dispersal, ignore, killing or shooting is established. Silence is retained as unknown.

notes: Actual march is reported, but “dozens” does not establish the >=50 criterion. No exact end or event-specific state response is documented. Separate Jan 9 search-only coverage says the plan was expanded to include Affordable Input Programme concerns before its Jan 13 postponement; whether that was also part of the final Jan 19 march is not established by the Jan 20 report.
open_questions: Determine whether turnout reached 50.
Clarify whether any formal state representative received or answered the group during this march.
Search follow-up for closure and related local actions.

title: Zomba female sex workers’ demonstration against Covid-19 guidelines
scope: Local Zomba action; relation to other sex-worker demonstrations is unresolved.
organizer: A group of concerned female sex workers; a representative is named as Gladys James.
threshold_50_evidence: Search-result text says a group took to the streets but provides no attendance estimate; at least 50 remains unverified.

occurrence.summary: Face of Malawi search-result article says a group of sex workers from Zomba took to the streets Wednesday morning. Underlying page not opened; occurrence remains pending_evidence.

start_date.summary: Article result is dated Jan 21 and describes the action as Wednesday morning, corresponding to Jan 20.

end_date.summary: No physical closure detail in the result.

organizer.summary: The article calls the group concerned sex workers and quotes representative Gladys James; no formal organization is named.

demands.summary: Oppose 8pm bar closure under Covid guidelines and ask government officials to consider economic concerns.

participants.summary: No attendance number in the result.

protester_violence.summary: No conduct detail in the result.

state_response.summary: Result says city officials turned the group back and requested written concerns. Treat as no receipt/accommodation at that encounter; no force, arrest, beating, ignore, killing or shooting detail.

notes: Search-result text identifies an actual local demonstration on Jan 20 and says officials turned the group back, asking that concerns be submitted in writing. The article body could not be retrieved; no attendance figure is given, so occurrence details and >=50 eligibility remain pending. Do not merge it with the Jan 28 Lilongwe FSWA action absent evidence of common organization/episode.
open_questions: Open the source or find contemporaneous Zomba reporting.
Establish exact date, actual assembly, attendance >=50, organizer, demands and state response.
Resolve whether part of a national FSWA action or a distinct local event.

title: Minibus drivers and conductors’ protest over fuel prices and passenger limits
location: Chikwawa, Mulanje, Blantyre (including Chirimba/Malandilova, Bangwe, Lunzu and Chilobwe), Zomba (including Chinamwali/M3), Lilongwe; Malawi24 also names Mwanza and other towns/districts.
scope: Multilocal action; whether one centrally organized national protest or several local actions is unresolved.
organizer: Minibus drivers and conductors; MDCA spokesperson said they acted, while MOAM representation and its involvement are disputed across reports.
threshold_50_evidence: No verified numerical count establishes 50 or more people; retain the reported qualitative wording and leave threshold unresolved.

occurrence.summary: Malawi24 and The Nation report actual Jan 26 protests, with minibuses parked/roadblocks and actions in multiple cities/districts. CIVICUS later summarizes the event and cites contemporaneous reporting; it is not counted as an independent witness.

start_date.summary: Both contemporary reports date the protests to Tuesday Jan 26.

end_date.summary: The article says the strike was called off, but gives no time or evidence that all local gatherings ended simultaneously.

location.summary: The Nation lists Chikwawa, Mulanje, Blantyre, Zomba and Lilongwe with neighborhood-level sites; Nyasa Times describes Chirimba/Malandilova, Bangwe and Chinamwali; Malawi24 additionally lists Mwanza and other areas.

organizer.summary: MDCA spokesperson Evans Galasi is quoted by Malawi24 and The Nation; Nyasa Times includes MOAM southern leadership. The Nation quotes MOAM national chair denying MOAM organized the action. Preserve organizational dispute.

demands.summary: Lower fuel prices and allow three passengers per seat despite Covid capacity restrictions; sources differ on whether an earlier three-per-seat agreement existed and who was bound by it.

participants.summary: No protester count. Nyasa Times reports over 100 police officers on the ground, which is not participant attendance; parked minibuses/affected commuters also are not converted to a crowd estimate.

protester_violence.summary: The Nation reports drivers/conductors throwing stones at motorists in some cases and a spokesperson alleges outsiders hijacked some conduct. Nyasa Times reports operators attacking motorbike kabaza drivers at Bangwe. Attributed conduct is reported but its distribution and organizer attribution remain contested.

state_response.summary: Malawi24, Nation and Nyasa Times report police tear gas used to disperse road-blocking drivers in Blantyre/Zomba (crowd_dispersal yes). No event-specific arrests, beatings, killings or shootings established. A government/association agreement and ongoing engagement are reported with conflicting timing/organizations, so accommodation remains unknown.

notes: Actual multiregional public protest is corroborated by two contemporary outlets; neither reports turnout. At least one reports tear gas. One reports stones thrown at motorists but includes a disputed attribution. The episode’s geographic and organizational boundaries and any prior December action need review. Nyasa Times reports >100 police at the scene; this is police presence, not a protester count. It also reports attacks on kabaza operators at a Bangwe roadblock; The Nation reports stone throwing at motorists and quotes a spokesperson alleging outsiders hijacked some conduct.
open_questions: Establish crowd size without substituting number of vehicles or drivers in a labor group.
Resolve association, government-agreement, exact-site and physical-end conflicts.
Check whether any Dec 2020 action was continuous or separate.
Reconcile Nyasa Times’ MOAM southern spokesperson with The Nation’s report that MOAM denied involvement; do not infer central coordination from association names.

title: Female sex workers’ Lilongwe march against curfew and bar restrictions
scope: Local Lilongwe action; link to separately reported Zomba action unresolved.
participants_original: “dozens of sex workers” (The Guardian; no exact number reported)
threshold_50_evidence: No verified numerical count establishes 50 or more people; retain the reported qualitative wording and leave threshold unresolved.

occurrence.summary: The Guardian and Nyasa Times independently report an actual FSWA-led march in Lilongwe on Jan 28. Later CIVICUS/VOA summaries support the issue but are not treated as independent event witnesses; the Southern African Herald page is a Nyasa Times repost, and Dullah Omar cites The Guardian.

start_date.summary: Guardian identifies Thursday Jan 28; Nyasa Times reports the march on Jan 28.

end_date.summary: No physical closure or end time reported.

organizer.summary: Female Sex Workers Association (FSWA), led in the reports by Zinenani Majawa.

demands.summary: Review curfew and bar-closing rules; Guardian says FSWA sought later closing and weekend operations. Nyasa Times reports the District Commissioner declined to receive the petition, after which protesters went to the City Council; the council’s response is not reported.

participants.summary: The Guardian describes “dozens of sex workers”; no numeric range is stated, and association membership is not turnout.

protester_violence.summary: Neither contemporary report describes violence by marchers; silence does not establish no violence.

state_response.summary: The District Commissioner explicitly refused to receive the petition; ignore=yes is scoped to that refusal and accommodation=no_explicit at that office. The group then went to Lilongwe City Council; its receipt/outcome is unreported. Guardian says there was no immediate government comment on the petition but quotes Attorney General Chikosa Silungwe saying government would look at the issues and respond. That later media comment is not a documented formal meeting or City Council receipt; coordinator review may change the broader ignore coding. No event-specific police force, arrests, beatings, killings or shootings reported.

notes: The march is independently reported by Guardian and Nyasa Times. “Dozens” does not establish >=50. Earlier police abuse is reported as context/grievance, not as state violence at this gathering. State-response coding records the District Commissioner’s explicit refusal only; the City Council’s later receipt or answer is unknown and should not be generalized as a government-wide refusal. The Guardian reports an Attorney General statement that government would look at issues and respond; this is not a documented formal meeting or City Council receipt and is retained for coordinator review of state response.
open_questions: Verify whether the march included at least 50 actual participants.
Clarify whether the City Council received/responded to the petition and establish physical end.
Resolve whether the Zomba report reflects a separate local event or a coordinated action.
Review how the Attorney General’s later statement to the Guardian affects event-level ignore/accommodation coding, while keeping the refusal scoped to the District Commissioner.

title: AHL employees’ announced demonstration over unpaid salaries
scope: Planned local demonstration; no evidence establishes whether it occurred or was coordinated elsewhere.
threshold_50_evidence: No verified numerical count establishes 50 or more people; retain the reported qualitative wording and leave threshold unresolved.

occurrence.summary: Malawi24 archive search result announces a Monday demonstration in Lilongwe over unpaid wages, intended Jan 4. Jan 6 Malawi24 does not confirm execution or cancellation. Biz Malawi says workers had demonstrated during arrears since Sep 2020 but does not date those actions precisely; these could be pre-month.

start_date.summary: The archive search result announces a Monday plan in Lilongwe, corresponding to Jan 4, but physical occurrence is unverified. Leave event start unknown; retain the announced date in notes.

end_date.summary: No evidence of execution or closure; leave unknown.

location.summary: Archive result says the demonstration was planned in Lilongwe.

organizer.summary: AHL employees are named in the announcement.

demands.summary: Unpaid salaries are reported. Whether workers directed a demand to the national government, rather than AHL as employer, is unresolved.

participants.summary: No attendance estimate; only an announcement is available.

protester_violence.summary: Occurrence and conduct were not verified.

state_response.summary: No executed gathering or event-specific response is established.

notes: The date Jan 4 is the announced/proposed date from a search-only archive entry, not a verified physical start. A Jan 6 salary-payment follow-up does not confirm occurrence or cancellation. The demand may have been directed to AHL as employer; government targeting is unresolved.
open_questions: Find contemporaneous evidence that the Jan 4 gathering occurred or was cancelled.
Establish whether the demand targeted the state, whether >=50 assembled, and whether this action is distinct from undated Sep–Dec 2020 demonstrations.
